title: SCAMMER CALLS PRANKSTER - Microsoft Tech Support Scam
description: This scammer called the wrong guy by calling me.  I drove him crazy by pretending to be computer illiterate and not letting him get his way.  I eventually let him talk to my twin brother who's really good with computers but doesn't have the patience.  It goes back and forth until the scammer finally loses it and hangs up.  For those wondering, the call was real.  I just reenacted later for the visuals in hopes to make it funnier.  Check out my playlist of other calls from scammers and telemarketers: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL47zBowjY-26vLDCKG-MsmopItZwu8V3w  Check out my new channel starring my dog (ChumpieTheDog) in some hilarious and cute videos  - http://bit.ly/1YqLXiu

The source does not establish whether the caller's claimed service identity was genuine or whether the interaction was promotional, deceptive, or demonstrative beyond that attribution.
textual.potential_relevance: The claimed technical-support identity is linked to requests to operate and connect the audience's computer, which warrants later assessment of what access, authorization, or destination the caller was seeking.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish that remote access occurred, that software was installed, that credentials or payment were requested, or that any loss resulted.

evidence.quote: For those wondering, the call was real. I just reenacted later for the visuals in hopes to make it funnier.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because its primary purpose is prank commentary about a reported technical-support call, with the creator frustrating the caller and reenacting the visuals for humor rather than presenting the caller's service as his own offer.
